title: EXISTS vs COUNT(*) for Existence Checks
description: Using COUNT(*) > 0 to test existence reads all matching rows; IF EXISTS / EXISTS stops at the first match.
narrative:
## Scenario
A dashboard needs to know *whether* a customer segment has any open orders. The code asks `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Orders WHERE Status = 'Open'` and then checks `> 0`.

## Why it's slow
`COUNT(*)` must read **every** matching row to count them. With ~66,000 open orders, SQL Server seeks into the `Status` index and then scans the entire `'Open'` range — hundreds of logical reads — just to answer a yes/no question.

## What to look for
- In `STATISTICS IO`: logical reads proportional to the number of matching rows.
- The plan does a range seek **plus** a Stream Aggregate over the whole range.

## The concept
When you only need to know *if any* rows exist, `EXISTS` (or `IF EXISTS`) **short-circuits** — it stops at the first matching row. The engine seeks to the first `'Open'` order and returns immediately, reading only a few pages regardless of how many matches there are.
startingQuery: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Orders WHERE Status = 'Open';
hints: You don't need the exact count — only whether at least one open order exists.
COUNT(*) reads every matching row; EXISTS stops at the first one it finds.
Use IF EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Orders WHERE Status = 'Open') ... to short-circuit.
